title: Technical reference: adult algorithm
text: EWMA: Exponentially Weighted Moving Average — weighted average subject’s weight measurements, measurements closer time receive exponentially weight. exponent e=−5, making nearest neighbor almost entirely dominant; closer near-neighbor comparison traditional moving average. Three variants computed observation: ewma_all (values), ewma_before (excluding immediately preceding value), ewma_after (excluding immediately following value). /variants used confirmation — value excluded overall directional deviations agree. Edge values (first/last subject) one neighbor, /falls back ewma_all. Window parameter ewma_window (default 15) limits many observations side contribute. Ordered steps: Removing extreme problems first, getting refined end Iterations: Many exclusion steps use dynamic loop: one value excluded per round (worst candidate defined scoring rule), EWMA thresholds recomputed scratch remaining values, process repeats. loop runs candidates remain fewer 3 values left. single-worst--per-round approach prevents cluster outliers masking — removing deviant value first often exposes next, appeared plausible evaluated simultaneously. Exclusion rescue: adult algorithm rescue exclusions way child algorithm rescues carried-forward values. one exception moderate EWMA step (11Wb): 4 consecutive candidates found single pass, excluded -Error-Load code rather one per round (linked mode, RV copies, subject’s remaining weights excluded). treats long run EWMA failures evidence overall data unreliability rather sequence isolated errors. Flexibility: Defaults looser (moderate permissiveness). Can made permissive (loosest) restrictive (tighter, tightest). Missing measurements: row whose measurement missing (NA/NaN — parameter row present data carrying value, including 0 converted NaN upstream) set aside (reported Exclude-Missing-Info) cleaning step runs participate step. matters algorithm derives quantities measurements (BMI -day height+weight pair, EWMA deviations, medians) compares thresholds; missing value left play propagate NA comparisons. rows removed per-subject height weight working sets entry, never -day BMI partner never enter trajectory. reported Exclude-Missing-Info final output. text: threshold comparisons algorithm apply 0.12 unit tolerance (cm height, kg weight). accommodates rounding may occur data extraction, transformation, loading — specifically, rounding nearest 0.1 cm 0.1 kg, plus small margin floating-point precision. tolerance makes threshold comparisons slightly permissive: value must exceed limit 0.12 excluded. example, PIV minimum height 50 cm, recorded value 49.9 cm excluded (within 0.12 threshold). comparing two measured values (e.g., height difference band check), tolerance applied (0.12), doubled. tolerance applied: PIV limits (Adult Step 1): value vs fixed min/max thresholds Weight cap EWMA checks (Adult Step 4W): dewma_all vs 50 kg; dewma_before/dewma_after vs 45 kg (0.9 factor applied 50 kg base); adjacency diffs vs 50 kg Evil twins caps (Adult Step 9Wa): weight difference vs dynamic cap Extreme EWMA (Adult Step 9Wb): dewma vs dynamic threshold Height distinct (Adult Steps 10Ha/10Hb): band checks, gain/loss direction rescue Weight 2D ordered non-ordered (Adult Steps 11Wa/11Wa2): weight difference vs wtallow Moderate EWMA (Adult Step 11Wb): dewma vs wtallow (standard alternate pathways) 1D limits (Adult Step 13): value vs fixed min/max thresholds tolerance applied: BMI thresholds (derived ht+wt; 0.12 either produces <0.1 BMI unit change) Perclimit ratio checks (conversion factors cancel ratios) Error load ratio (Adult Step 14; count-based, measurement-based) Exact equality checks (RV identification, SDE identical detection — conversion applied uniformly, identical inputs produce identical outputs)

title: Technical reference: adult algorithm
text: Purpose. Three functions interval- weight-based thresholds used across multiple steps. compute_wtallow() computes maximum plausible weight change given interval , optionally, upper weight (UW). compute_et_limit() computes Evil Twins / extreme EWMA cap (wtallow-cap + 20 kg PW-H/PW-L; allofus15 12-month cap allofus15; fixed 70/100 custom CSV). compute_perc_limit() returns observation-level percentage ratio threshold tiered weight. See wtallow section full formula derivations design rationale. Callers. compute_wtallow() called cleanadult() (Adult Steps 11Wa 11Wa2) evil_twins(), remove_ewma_wt(), remove_mod_ewma_wt(). compute_et_limit() called evil_twins() remove_ewma_wt(). compute_perc_limit() called remove_mod_ewma_wt(). Inputs return contract. compute_wtallow(months, formula = "piecewise", uw = NULL) — months numeric vector interval lengths months; formula "piecewise" (PW-H), "piecewise-lower" (PW-L), "allofus15", file path custom CSV columns months wtallow; uw optional upper-weight vector (NULL = base, UW = 120). Returns numeric vector weight allowances. compute_et_limit(interval_months, formula = "piecewise", uw = NULL) — signature; returns ET caps. Two-tier output: ≤ 6 months → et_6m cap, > 6 months → et_12m cap (except allofus15, flat across intervals). compute_perc_limit(meas, perclimit_low, perclimit_mid, perclimit_high) — vectorized meas (weight kg). Returns perclimit_low meas ≤ 45, perclimit_mid 45 < meas ≤ 80, perclimit_high meas > 80. Key mechanics wtallow formulas section. three formulas cap uw_eff 180 kg via pmin(uw, 180) applying scale factors. Custom CSV path: file loaded cached package-internal environment .gc_cache .wtallow_custom_cache; path attribute cache detects different file passed. side effect persists across cleangrowth() calls within R session. compute_et_limit() allofus15: returns flat value (allofus15 12-month cap UW) regardless interval — unlike PW-H/PW-L ≤ 6m / > 6m tiers. Code location. R/adult_support.R (compute_et_limit, compute_perc_limit, compute_wtallow).

title: Technical reference: adult algorithm
text: Purpose. Three helpers supporting Adult Step 10H (Height Distinct Values). ht_allow(velocity, ageyears1, ageyears2) computes maximum expected height gain age range using log-based growth model. ht_change_groups(h_subj_df, cutoff, type) groups consecutive height measurements within 2 inches (5.08 + 0.12 cm rounding tolerance) ; exits early measurement diverges 2 inches current group specified direction. ht_3d_growth_compare(mean_ht, min_age, glist, compare) checks whether adjacent height groups plausible height differences, applying velocity tiers based inter-group age gap, 25-year age cap. Callers. three called exclusively cleanadult() Adult Step 10H block. ht_allow() called within ht_3d_growth_compare(). Inputs return contract. ht_allow(velocity, ageyears1, ageyears2) — three scalars; returns scalar. Formula: velocity × (log(ageyears2 – 16.9) – log(ageyears1 – 16.9)). Undefined ageyears ≤ 16.9 — safe practice adult algorithm processes ages adult_cutpoint (18–20 years). ht_change_groups(h_subj_df, cutoff, type = "loss") — h_subj_df pre-sorted age; cutoff maximum number groups form; type = "loss" exits early measurement drops > 5.08 + 0.12 cm current group minimum, type = "gain" exits measurement rises > 5.08 + 0.12 cm current group maximum. Returns list entries "meas" (list named numeric vectors, names = internal_id) "age" (list age vectors). Returns empty lists early-exit condition fires completing groups. ht_3d_growth_compare(mean_ht, min_age, glist, compare = "") — mean_ht min_age numeric vectors indexed group; compare = "" checks group immediately preceding group, compare = "first" checks first group. Velocity tiers: < 1-year gap → 20 cm/yr, 1–3 year gap → 15 cm/yr, > 3-year gap → 12 cm/yr. Comparison age capped 25 years. Returns single boolean: TRUE adjacent pair fails velocity check. Key invariants. ht_3d_growth_compare() skips groups indexed beyond length(glist) via next, short group lists safe. 0.12 cm rounding tolerance applied 5.08 cm (2-inch) threshold ht_change_groups(). height loss/gain check uses mh2 – mh1 relative zero hta, 0.12 tolerance applied bounds. Code location. R/adult_support.R.

Deleting is #    always safe: growthcleanr falls back to its default when a setting is gone. # ============================================================================  install.packages("growthcleanr")             # first time only library(growthcleanr) library(data.table)  df <- fread("my_growth_data.csv")             # your file name  cleaned <- cleangrowth(   # to check your setup first, change "cleangrowth" to "gc_runtrial"   df,    # ==========================================================================   #  PERFORMANCE  -- worth setting before a large run (see the   #  "Large datasets" article for full guidance)   # ==========================================================================    # PARALLEL: use several CPU cores at once. FALSE (default) uses one core.   # For more than a few thousand subjects, set this to TRUE.   parallel = FALSE,          # change to TRUE to speed up large datasets   cores    = NULL,           # NULL auto-detects (up to 8); or set a number like 4    # CHECKPOINTING: clean large data in pieces so the run stays fast and within   # memory; name a folder to also make the run resumable if it is interrupted.   # Leave NULL: checkpointing is automatic for more than 5,000 subjects   # (temporary files, deleted after). Name a folder only to keep the files   # for resuming.   checkpoint_dir    = NULL,  # e.g. "gc_checkpoints"                               # if the folder does not exist, growthcleanr will make it                              # existing checkpoint files in this folder are deleted at the start, unless checkpoint_resume = TRUE   checkpoint_resume = FALSE, # set TRUE to resume that folder after a crash    # ==========================================================================   #  COLUMN NAMES  -- left = what growthcleanr expects, right = YOUR column name   # ==========================================================================   subjid      = "subjid",       # subject id (one person)   id          = "id",           # optional per-ROW id; delete this line if you have none   param       = "param",        # which measurement (weight/height/head circ.)   agedays     = "agedays",      # age in days (delete this line if you use DATES below)   sex         = "sex",   measurement = "measurement",    # ==========================================================================   #  SEX CODING   #  Default: male = 0,"m","b","male","boy"; female = 1,"f","g","female","girl"   #  IMPORTANT: growthcleanr reads 1 as FEMALE. If your data uses 1 = male,   #  2 = female, you MUST set this. Whatever you put here REPLACES the defaults,   #  so list every code you use. Delete this line to keep the defaults.   # ==========================================================================   sex_coding = list(male   = c(0, "m", "b", "male", "boy"),                     female = c(1, "f", "g", "female", "girl")),    # ==========================================================================   #  MEASUREMENT-TYPE (param) CODING   #  growthcleanr recognizes only these spelled-out labels:   #    WEIGHTKG, WEIGHTLBS, HEIGHTCM, HEIGHTIN, LENGTHCM, LENGTHIN, HEADCM, HEADIN   #  If your data uses other labels (e.g. WT/HT/HC), map them here. Mapping to an   #  imperial name (WEIGHTLBS/HEIGHTIN/...) also tells growthcleanr the units.   #  EXAMPLE (default is NULL): map your own labels.   #  Delete this line if your labels already match the names above.   # ==========================================================================   param_coding = list(WEIGHTKG = c("WT", "Weight"),                       HEIGHTCM = c("HT", "Height"),                       HEADCM   = c("HC", "HeadCirc")),    # ==========================================================================   #  DATES INSTEAD OF agedays  (optional)   #  Most people supply age in days and can DELETE this whole section.   #  To use dates instead: fill in your two date columns below AND delete the   #  `agedays` line up in COLUMN NAMES. growthcleanr computes age from the dates.   #  Text dates like "2013-03-04" or "15 Mar 2013" work with no extra setting.   #  For number dates like "3/4/2013", set date_order to "mdy" or "dmy".   # ==========================================================================   dob        = NULL,   # e.g. "birth_date"   visit_date = NULL,   # e.g. "measure_date"   date_order = NULL,   # e.g. "mdy" (US) or "dmy" -- only for number dates    quietly = FALSE      # FALSE prints a progress + cleaning summary; TRUE stays silent )  # --- Save the cleaned results ----------------------------------------------- fwrite(cleaned, "my_growth_data_cleaned.csv") library(growthcleanr) library(data.table) df <- fread("my_growth_data.csv")  # Left = the name growthcleanr uses; columns like wt_1, ht_1, wt_2, ...  cleaned <- cleangrowth(   # to check your setup first, change "cleangrowth" to "gc_runtrial"   df,   input_format = "wide",   # Give the column-name PREFIX for each measurement type (the part before _N).   # Delete this line if your prefixes are already WEIGHTKG / HEIGHTCM / HEADCM.   wide_cols = list(WEIGHTKG = "wt", HEIGHTCM = "ht", HEADCM = "hc") ) fwrite(cleaned, "my_growth_data_cleaned.csv") library(growthcleanr) library(data.table) df <- fread("my_growth_data.csv")  cleaned <- cleangrowth(   # to check your setup first, change "cleangrowth" to "gc_runtrial"   df,   exclude_detail = TRUE   # adds a finer-grained "exclude_detailed" column ) fwrite(cleaned, "my_growth_data_cleaned.csv") library(growthcleanr) library(data.table) df <- fread("my_growth_data.csv")  cleaned <- cleangrowth(   # to check your setup first, change "cleangrowth" to "gc_runtrial"   df,   adult_cutpoint       = 20,        # age in years when the adult algorithm takes over (18-20)   adult_permissiveness = "looser"   # loosest to tightest; title: Exclusion codes
text: growthcleanr reports value one multiple verbosity levels: Summary (default) — value exclude column. Consolidated across steps across child/adult algorithms; smallest useful reason set typical user. 14 codes. Detailed (opt-via exclude_detail = TRUE full_detail = TRUE) — adds exclude_detailed column. Step-level; keeps child (-C-) / adult (--) algorithm prefix; folds away repeated-value (RV / firstRV / allRV), -, round-iteration distinctions. Every Detailed code maps exactly one Summary code. text: Calling styles: Data-frame style (recommended). Pass single data.frame data.table data. subjid, param, agedays, sex, measurement, id arguments column-name strings identifying columns data use. defaults canonical name (e.g. "subjid"), columns already use names can just call cleangrowth(data = my_df). Use column-name arguments remap (e.g. subjid = "patid"). Vector style (legacy). Omit data pass subjid, param, agedays, sex, measurement vector. Retained backward compatibility existing code; new code use data-frame style. vectors (columns referenced data) must length aligned row--row. Pulling values different datasets supported checked . Arguments glance. many arguments fall groups; runs touch first one two: Core input column names – data, subjid, sex, agedays, param, measurement, id. Age dates (instead agedays) – dob, visit_date, age_source, date_order. Sex parameter coding – sex_coding, param_coding. Input/output shape – input_format, output_format, semiwide_cols, wide_cols, max_blocks, widened_emit, carry_through. Run control performance – parallel, cores, batch_size, quietly, verbose, ref_tables, ref.data.path, log.path. Checkpointed (resumable) runs – checkpoint, checkpoint_dir, checkpoint_size, checkpoint_resume, keep_checkpoints, log_file. Adult algorithm – adult_cutpoint, adult_permissiveness, adult_scale_max_lbs, adult_overrides. EWMA window (child adult) – ewma_window. Length vs. height handling – length.adjust. Recentering – sd.recenter. Carried-forward rescue – cf_rescue. Optional output columns – exclude_detail, unit_error_range, tri_exclude, cf_detail, corr_detail, recenter_detail, internal_detail, display_gc_id, mean_ht, full_detail, qm_detail, debug. title: growthcleanr 3.0.0
text: Algorithms. Multiple changes improve performance, including: updated child algorithm improved handling infants cleaning head circumference age 5 years; updated adult algorithm four permissiveness levels; new “evil twins” step detect runs consecutive erroneous values; rescue many consecutive identical values previously excluded carried forward; built-recentering medians based clinical data. Input. cleangrowth() accepts data frame, option use alternate column names. Data can one three formats: long (one measurement per row), semi-wide (one visit per row), wide (one subject per row). Users may enter date birth visit date rather agedays. optional id column makes results fully replicable. Shiny app also handles formats dates. ready--run scripts, see vignette("example-scripts"); full detail, see “Input format: long, semi-wide, wide” “Date parsing” vignette("wrapper"). Output. cleangrowth() returns data results added. New outputs include redesigned exclusion codes bin_exclude, unit_error_range, mean_ht columns. Efficiency. Checkpointing, default datasets 5,000 subjects, reduces memory use keeps run time roughly linear number subjects. Parallel processing simpler use (parallel = TRUE). gc_partial_run() re-cleans subjects whose data changed. Trial runs. gc_runtrial() runs growthcleanr sample data reports columns, sex coding, parameters read, can check setup full run. Documentation. -guides Shiny app R interface, researcher overview, fact sheet, ready--run scripts (vignette("example-scripts")), expanded technical documentation.

title: growthcleanr 3.0.0
text: Code written 2.2.3 need updated. apologize inconvenience causes experienced users hope changes make growthcleanr easier users. Details replacement code “Updating code written growthcleanr 2.2.3” vignette("experienced-start-"). Results differ 2.2.3, setting reproduces 2.2.3 exactly. reproduce analysis done 2.2.3, keep using 2.2.3. cleangrowth() takes data frame first argument returns data.table, vector exclusion codes. content old vector now exclude column. Old calls unnamed arguments stop message, code names arguments treats result vector can run without error give wrong results. Exclusion codes renamed meaningful. Filters specific 2.2.3 codes match anything, without warning. See “Mapping prior exclusion codes” vignette("experienced-start-"). growthcleanr now excludes subset consecutive identical values, controlled new cf_rescue argument. testacf() acf_answers() removed, adjustcarryforward() now stops message. See vignette("cf-rescue"). Several arguments removed renamed, removed argument stops message naming use instead. example, num.batches now cores, weight_cap kg now adult_scale_max_lbs pounds. See “Removed renamed arguments” vignette("experienced-start-"). sd.recenter argument still allows users enter recentering table. default, sd.recenter = NA, growthcleanr now uses built-recentering table based clinical data. "nhanes" "derive" options sd_median() removed. See vignette("recentering"). splitinput() removed; checkpointing replaces . See vignette("large-datasets"). command-line driver moved (find gc_cli_path()) accepts long flags. See vignette("command-line"). ext_bmiz() output keeps column names, longwide() arguments changed. avoid errors related numeric sex coding, longwide() now returns sex M F, numeric sex, filters longwide() output sex == 1 sex == 2 match rows, without warning. ext_bmiz() now stops numeric sex unless sex 1s 2s values. See vignette("utilities"). Docker support dropped.
